hook.line: When someone does the same annoying thing for the hundredth time, you don't need a whole sentence. Spanish lets a single -ing word carry the sigh.

examples.en: Glued to your phone all day!
Arguing over the same thing again!

rule:
Put *siempre*, *otra vez*, *todo el día* or *todo el tiempo* in front of an -ing form (*-ando*, *-iendo*) and you have a complaint, with no conjugated verb at all. English does it too ("Always late!"), but Spanish makes it the normal way to sigh.

Who is doing it comes from the scene, or from a little word on the end: *quejándote* (you), *quejándome* (me), *quejándonos* (us).

It is sharp when said to someone's face. To soften it, use a real verb: *Perdón, pero es que siempre llegas tarde.*
smallPrint: Teachers call this a gerund used on its own as an exclamation. The *-ándote* ending is the gerund with a pronoun attached, which is why it carries a written accent.

options: You always arrive late. (to a friend)
He'll be glued to the phone tomorrow!
Glued to your phone all day!
I left my phone at home all day.
Arguing over the same thing again!

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *llegando* or *llegas* to make the outburst with no conjugated verb, and type the whole sentence: *¡Siempre ___ tarde!*
yourTurn.why: The outburst uses the bare -ing form, *llegando*, with no *tú* verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: You're complaining again! (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Otra vez* plus the -ing form, and *-te* on the end tells us it is you.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Always looking at the phone!
yourTurn.why: *Siempre* plus *mirando*: no *estás*, no *está*, just the -ing form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Always blaming Vale!
yourTurn.why: The little word *le* sticks to the end of *echando*, so it gains a written accent.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about yourself: *¡Otra vez quejándote!* Say: I'm complaining again!
yourTurn.why: Swap *-te* for *-me* and the complaint turns on you.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Arguing over the same thing again!
yourTurn.why: *Otra vez* works just like *siempre* in front of the -ing form.

yourTurn.prompt: Soften it for a real conversation: *¡Siempre llegando tarde!* Say, to a friend: Sorry, but the thing is you always arrive late.
yourTurn.answer: Perdón, pero es que siempre llegas tarde.
yourTurn.why: A real verb, *llegas*, plus *perdón, pero es que* is gentler than the bare outburst.

pitfalls.why: Almost. English 'always to arrive' tempts the plain verb, but the outburst needs the -ing form, *llegando*.
Almost. *Quejarse* needs its little word, *-te* for you or *-me* for me, so we know who is complaining.
That is correct Spanish, but this pattern drops *estás* entirely: the bare -ing form is what makes it an outburst.

personal: Think of one thing you do again and again, then say it as a sigh at yourself: *¡Otra vez ...ndo!* Then say the gentle version you would use with a friend: *Perdón, pero es que siempre ...*
